newsitem.title: FINLAND: UPM-Kymmene CEO sees newsprint downside.
newsitem.headline: UPM-Kymmene CEO sees newsprint downside.

text.p: Juha Niemela, CEO at UPM-Kymmene Oy, a major supplier of paper for Europe's print media, on Thursday said the company should be fully aware of the risk newsprint prices may fall next year.

"We shouldn't underestimate it," he told a news conference when asked if he saw a risk of newsprint prices falling in 1997. Niemela said the risk was there because prices in Europe were still higher than elsewhere, but he did not elaborate.
The company said in its January-August report it had been forced by oversupply to lower newsprint prices "on some markets" during the summer, and prices were still falling slightly.
It said demand for newsprint in western Europe fell by five percent, but reported better January-August operating profits in newsprint thanks to January price hikes.
"In the USA, demand fell by 10 percent, prompting Canadian suppliers to step up their exports to Europe," UPM-Kymmene said.
At the same time, Canada's export markets in Southeast Asia were shrinking as new capacity comes onstream.

"The rise in imports has caused European manufacturers to lose some of their share of the market," it said. It did not comment on its own market share position, but said its newsprint production fell by nine percent.

UPM-Kymmene said its January-August capacity utilisation rate in newsprint was 86 percent. It did not give a comparison, but said in June its newsprint capacity use in January-April had been 93 percent.
Niemela told the news conference UPM-Kymmmene's newsprint capacity use for the rest of this year would be around 90 percent.
"In newsprint, stoppages will continue so capacity use is likely to be at the 90 percent level," he said.
